clue.text: Very small house in central London location

parts.note: very and so are interchangeable intensifiers, as in 'so tired'
HO is the standard written abbreviation of house, so a shortened (small) house

explanation.surface: A tiny dwelling somewhere in the heart of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very small' reads as one phrase about the house's size; split it so 'Very' gives SO and 'small house' gives HO, the abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A district of the West End, famed for nightlife and media firms, so a place in central London.

clue.text: Mail is distributed by society for principle of equal distribution

indicators.note: letters that are distributed are dealt out in a new order, so the fodder is rearranged

explanation.surface: Post shared out by an organisation that believes everything should be shared fairly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distributed' does double duty in the surface, echoing the definition's 'distribution', but signals the anagram; the society abbreviation comes first though printed last.
explanation.definitionFit: The political doctrine of common ownership aims at sharing wealth fairly across the community.

clue.text: Gives workers pointers

definitions.meaning: to pass something over to someone, as in passing a plate across
manual labourers on a farm or in a factory, as in 'all aboard, crew'
the indicators that move round a clock face

explanation.surface: Someone passes useful tips to the staff.
explanation.walkthrough: Three definitions run together: a verb and two plural nouns, all the same word.
explanation.definitionFit: The one word means passes over, farm or factory labourers, and the moving arms of a clock.

clue.text: Time with number one is precious

parts.note: number one is a childish euphemism for urinating, as is wee

explanation.surface: Spending time with yourself as the top priority is valuable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number one' looks like self-interest; it is the nursery euphemism for a pee.
explanation.definitionFit: Precious in the sense of affectedly dainty or sentimental, overly sweet and quaint.

clue.text: Capital way you and I lobby to cover up assassination

indicators.note: the outer word is wrapped round the other, covering it

parts.note: you and I together make we
a hit is a contract killing
a lobby is an entrance hall

explanation.surface: A conspiracy in the capital where we push to hush up a murder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital way' is a London street of ministries; 'to cover up' signals one piece wrapped around another, not concealment.
explanation.definitionFit: A London street lined with government ministries, so a road in the capital.

clue.text: United dropped out of league after replacing winger

indicators.note: once that letter is gone, one remaining letter is put back in a different place
the letter for United leaves the word league

parts.note: U is the usual abbreviation of United in team names

explanation.surface: A football club is relegated, and a wide player is swapped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dropped out of' takes U from LEAGUE, leaving LEAGE; 'after replacing' moves its L to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A winger is anything with wings, here a large bird of prey.

clue.text: Prisoner's accommodation has zero means of producing music

parts.note: an inmate is housed in a cell
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A jail room has nothing in it to make music with.
explanation.definitionFit: A large bowed string instrument, an obvious device for making music.

clue.text: Fail to impress censor with advertisement lacking tiniest bit of truth

parts.note: a censor cuts material

indicators.note: the advert goes without the letter named next

parts.note: a notice is a public announcement or advert

indicators.note: the smallest part of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A censor is unimpressed by an advert with hardly any truth in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking' removes the letter given by 'tiniest bit of truth' from the advert word; the result follows the censor's word.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning to have no effect or make no impression on someone.

clue.text: State obsessive about holding onto agreements from Paris and Madrid

indicators.note: the outer word grips the others inside it
about signals the word is turned round

parts.note: anal is slang for obsessively fussy
oui is French for yes
si is Spanish for yes, the agreement from Madrid

explanation.surface: A fixated person clinging to treaties made in two European capitals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agreements' are the words for yes in French and Spanish; 'about' turns the obsessive word round and 'holding onto' wraps it round them.
explanation.definitionFit: A southern US state on the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: A half-sibling joins love somewhere in the desert

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
sis is a sister, one kind of sibling, short form

explanation.surface: A step-relative falls in love in some arid region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-sibling' suggests a step-brother; it is SIS, a sister, roughly half of the sibling kinds.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot with water in an arid region.

clue.text: Manuscript covering evil factories

indicators.note: the abbreviation wraps round the other word

parts.note: ill can mean evil, as in 'ill deeds'

explanation.surface: A document concealing wicked industrial works.
explanation.definitionFit: Mills are industrial works such as cotton or paper plants.

clue.text: Sharing details of secret study hit after providing returns

indicators.note: the word for hit is placed after the rest

parts.note: to con is to study or learn by heart

indicators.note: the word for providing comes back, read backwards

parts.note: if means providing, as in 'providing that'
a ding is a blow or knock

explanation.surface: Revealing the findings of a confidential investigation that paid off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition takes four words; 'secret study' looks like a unit but 'study' starts the wordplay. 'returns' reverses 'providing' and 'after' places the blow last.
explanation.definitionFit: To confide is to share a private matter, so revealing something told in confidence.

clue.text: Bundle bursts badly after top of buckle goes

indicators.note: letters arranged badly are jumbled into a new order
the named letter leaves the word
the top of a word in a down-or-across sense is its first letter

explanation.surface: A bundle splits open when the buckle fastening fails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes' removes B ('top of buckle') from BURSTS, and 'badly' rearranges URSTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A truss is a tied bundle, especially of hay or straw.

clue.text: Forgive sailor's fickle love

parts.note: AB is an able seaman; with the possessive it gives ABS

indicators.note: something fickle keeps changing, so the letters change order

explanation.surface: A seaman's inconstant affections in every port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fickle' looks like a description of the sailor's love; it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: To pardon or clear someone of blame or sin, as a priest does.

clue.text: Those glorying in self-love die first in El Salvador

indicators.note: the pieces go inside the country code

parts.note: ES is the international code for El Salvador
to go is to die, as in 'when I go'
1ST, with I for the digit one

explanation.surface: Narcissists perish first in a Central American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' gives 1ST, with the digit read as the letter I; 'in' places the pieces inside the country code.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-centred people preoccupied with their own importance.

clue.text: Dodgy fellows found in Italy's borders

indicators.note: the pair of letters sits inside the border letters
a country's borders are its outer edges, so its first and last letters

parts.note: F is an abbreviation of fellow; doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Shady men turn up at an Italian frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'borders' takes I and Y from Italy; 'found in' puts FF between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal for doubtful or suspect, of questionable quality.

clue.text: Traps where prey flaps wildly

indicators.note: flapping wildly scatters these letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Snares in which a caught creature beats its wings frantically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges PREY FLAPS; the surface describes the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Sticky sheets hung up to catch insects, so traps.

clue.text: Stuff brill with syrup fried peacock hearts

parts.note: brill and fab are both slang for brilliant

indicators.note: the heart of each word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: A grotesque recipe: a flatfish with syrup and a fried peacock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brill' looks like the fish; it is slang for wonderful, FAB. 'hearts' takes R, I and C from the middles.
explanation.definitionFit: Stuff as a noun means material or cloth.

clue.text: Two records with X Factor backing get touching welcome

parts.note: REC is short for record and EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: backing means read backwards

parts.note: the X factor is that special quality, also called 'it'
on can mean touching, as in 'hand on shoulder'

explanation.surface: Two singles helped by a TV talent show earn a moving greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'X Factor' looks like the TV talent show; it is IT, star quality, and 'backing' reverses it to TI.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception is the way someone is greeted, or a formal party of welcome.

clue.text: Nakedly desires one living in colonies

indicators.note: stripped naked, the word loses its outer covering, its first and last letters

parts.note: wants means desires

explanation.surface: Someone's unashamed longings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nakedly' strips W and S from WANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A social insect that lives in large organised nests, so a colony dweller.

clue.text: Unending indulgence more certain for one in charge of funds

indicators.note: without its ending, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a treat is an indulgence
surer means more certain

explanation.surface: Endless self-indulgence is guaranteed for whoever controls the money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unending' cuts the last T from TREAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer who manages a club's or organisation's money.

clue.text: Chancellor of the Exchequer follows gold stamp with note to listeners

indicators.note: the abbreviation comes after the other pieces

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
a die is a tool for stamping coins or patterns
CE is an abbreviation for the UK finance minister's title

explanation.surface: The finance minister follows up a gold seal with a message to his listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chancellor of the Exchequer is Britain's finance minister, abbreviated CE; 'follows' puts it after AU, DIE and N.
explanation.definitionFit: The people gathered to hear a performance or speech.

clue.text: Could possibly mollify aggressive Yemeni leaders

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their opening letters

explanation.surface: Perhaps one could pacify hostile chiefs in Yemen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' looks like Yemeni rulers; it takes the first letters of three words.
explanation.definitionFit: A modal verb of possibility, as in 'it might rain'.

clue.text: No luck engendering release

indicators.note: engendering means producing, so the letters produce a new word

explanation.surface: Bad fortune leads to someone's freedom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engendering' rearranges NO LUCK.
explanation.definitionFit: To open a lock, freeing whatever was fastened.

clue.text: Wind insulation around end of pipe

indicators.note: around signals the word is turned the other way

parts.note: lagging is insulation; to lag pipes is to insulate them

indicators.note: the end of a word is its last letter

explanation.surface: Lagging wrapped round the end of a plumbing pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal; here it turns the insulation word back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong wind, between a stiff breeze and a storm.

clue.text: A politician joins special constable to get rogue

parts.note: SC abbreviates special constable, a volunteer police officer in Britain
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician teams up with a volunteer police officer to catch a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: A special constable is a part-time volunteer police officer in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous rascal, a playful rogue.

clue.text: Fire container constructed from prickly shrub containing core of monazite

indicators.note: the shrub holds the letters inside it

parts.note: a brier is a thorny bush

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle letters

explanation.surface: A recipe for a fireplace built from thorn bushes and a mineral.
explanation.walkthrough: Monazite is a phosphate mineral; 'core of' takes its two central letters and 'containing' puts them inside the shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal stand or basket holding burning coals.

clue.text: Foreign Office abandons legendary American primate fanatic

indicators.note: the abbreviation leaves the creature's name

parts.note: Bigfoot is the ape-like creature of North American folklore
FO is the UK Foreign Office

explanation.surface: The diplomatic service gives up on a mythical ape and its zealot.
explanation.walkthrough: The Foreign Office is Britain's foreign ministry, FO; 'abandons' takes it out of BIGFOOT.
explanation.definitionFit: An intolerant person with fixed prejudices, a fanatical partisan.

clue.text: Extend hand to every individual

parts.note: R stands for right, as in right hand
each means every individual one

explanation.surface: Offer a helping hand to everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extend hand' reads as one phrase; the definition is only 'Extend' and 'hand' gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: To stretch out an arm or to stretch as far as something.

clue.text: Relishes choice by the French

parts.note: a pick is a selection
les is French for the, plural

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys a selection of French dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relishes' looks like a verb; it is the noun, preserved condiments.
explanation.definitionFit: Relishes as nouns are chutneys and preserved condiments.

clue.text: Illegally kill wild cat taking tail for companion

indicators.note: the last letter is swapped for the letters that follow

parts.note: a lynx is a wild cat
CH is Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: A wild feline kills unlawfully and grabs its partner by the tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking tail for' swaps X, the tail of LYNX, for CH (Companion of Honour, a British award).
explanation.definitionFit: To execute someone by mob action without legal trial.

clue.text: Meagre enclosure holding Olive perhaps

indicators.note: the words hold the answer inside them, spread across both

explanation.surface: A small enclosed plot containing an olive tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olive' looks like a tree or a name; it is a shade of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is one shade of that colour, so an example.

clue.text: Turkey part a small child consumes one afternoon

indicators.note: the outer pieces take the inner ones inside

parts.note: a minor is a child in law
I is the Roman numeral one
A abbreviates afternoon, as in p.m. versus a.m. readings

explanation.surface: A little one gobbles a slice of turkey after lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turkey' suggests the bird; it is the country. 'consumes' puts IA inside A S MINOR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Anatolian peninsula, the Asian part of the country.

clue.text: Gallery hosts special experience

indicators.note: the gallery hosts, holding the letter inside

parts.note: the Tate is a group of British art galleries

explanation.surface: A gallery puts on a special event.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tate is a group of art galleries in London and elsewhere in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: To sample or experience something, as in a first sample of freedom.

clue.text: Adult dismissed from frequent search

indicators.note: the letter is sent out of the word

parts.note: to haunt a place is to frequent it
A is the film classification for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up is thrown out of a regular manhunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frequent' looks like an adjective; it is the verb, to haunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A search or pursuit, as for a missing person.

clue.text: Deity is interminable prick

indicators.note: without an end, the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a thorn is a sharp prickle

explanation.surface: A god turns out to be an endless irritant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interminable' looks like tedium; it means cut off the last letter, N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Norse god of thunder, wielder of a hammer.
